predicate.verdict_note: Second round on the T-1 parallel lanes. All five claimed fixes verified adversarially. (1) A lane that fails by itself is never STOPPED: STOPPED needs the mark and exit 128+TERM; a two-lanes-red-in-one-second probe now gives both RED, and the guard has a self-red case and a stopped-any-rc mutant it kills. (2) The parity lock is pinned structurally and the parity-unlocked mutant (flock to env) is killed. (3) Exit 75 now writes a reason that classify_parity_exit prints; measured. (4) Parity runs under choom; reads and runs. (5) The comment now says INT/TERM stops models. Still open, all advisory: INT/TERM still kills models and may orphan its remote leg (judged deliberate, documented; the guard does not pin it); a launch-window race of microseconds (judged acceptable); and the choom and the exit-75 reason have no test, since removing either leaves the guard at 11 of 11 killed.

findings.failure_scenario: A developer alters `t1_dogfood` to add a trailing space, or leaves a commented-out `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR` above the active one. The `awk` guard captures the differing full line strings, causing `[ "$d" != "$g" ]` to pass. Both lanes then build into the same shared target directory under the hood, causing Cargo to race on target artifacts and crash.
findings.summary: The `dirs()` check in the guard script extracts the target dir via `awk` as a full line string. It performs a strict string comparison without normalizing whitespace or ignoring comments, meaning lines that differ syntactically but resolve to the same path will bypass the collision check.

findings.failure_scenario: An operator or CI timeout sends `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` to the guard script (`check_release_t1_lanes_joined.sh`). The script exits and its `EXIT` trap cleans up `$TMP`, but the background processes spawned by `case_run` (running `harness.sh` and `sleep`) do not receive the signal and are left running as orphaned processes.
findings.summary: The `check_release_t1_lanes_joined.sh` guard script spawns background processes via `case_run() ... &` but lacks a trap for `INT` and `TERM` signals to terminate them upon premature exit.

findings.failure_scenario: The GPU lock is acquired successfully, but the underlying `$APR_BIN parity` payload fails internally and exits with `75` (e.g. `EX_TEMPFAIL`). The wrapper script misinterprets this as a lock timeout, appends the lock timeout error message to `$j.err`, and masks the actual model parity failure from the release operator.
findings.summary: In `check_model_parity.sh`, `flock` uses `-E 75` to indicate a lock timeout. If the `choom` wrapped command natively exits with code 75, the script will falsely attribute the failure to GPU lock contention.
